:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 08.12.2022 at about 5.00 p.m. petitioner along with his wife has been returning to home after grazing cattle and standing to cross the road at Mallarabhanawadi Gate, Nelamangala-Kunigal Highway, at that time, a Tata Ace Vehicle bearing Reg.NoKA-34-B- 1655 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was taken to Mathrushree Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, thereafter he took ayurvedic treatment, further he was shifted to M/s. Meditech Speciality Hospital, wherein also he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.
SCCH-5 3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 45 years, hale and healthy, he was doing milk vending business and real estate, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., due to this accident he has lost his good health and also his earnings.
Out of this accident crime No.518/2022 is registered against the driver of the said Tata Ace Vehicle before the Nelamangala Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the said Tata Ace Vehicle,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and stated that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act.

Further SCCH-5 submitted that, Tata Ace Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-34-B-1655 is not at all involved in the accident and petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional Police and owner of the vehicle has filed case.
Further submitted that, there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.
Further denied issuance of insurance policy to the said offending vehicle and its liability is subject to confirmation and terms and conditions of the policy.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
SCCH-5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.12.2022 at about 5.00 p.m. when the petitioner was returning home at Mallarabhanawadi ate, Nelamangala-Kunigal Highway, at that time, Tata Ace Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-34-B-1655 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6.

In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Rajesh M.B. Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW-2 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his SCCH-5 evidence.

On the other hand, authorized representative of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of charge sheet is SCCH-5 marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.10 and copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.11.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and his records those have marked i.e., as copy of charge sheet, FIR and complaint corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 08.12.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

On the other hand, authorized representative of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and he Anjan Murthy vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141019410/
3 has got exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.

sentences.text: Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement and oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove SCCH-5 the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 08.12.2022 at about 5.00 p.m. petitioner along with his wife has been returning to home after grazing cattle and standing to cross the road at Mallarabhanawadi Gate, Nelamangala- Kunigal Highway.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the Tata Ace Goods driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained posterior cruciate ligament injury left knee, for which he has undergone surgery i.e., arthroscopic PCL reconstruction left knee.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.1, discharge summary (2 in Nos.) marked as Ex.P.12 issued by Mathrushree Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient since 08.12.2022 to 10.12.2022 and discharge summary issued by Meditech Healthcare Group,
wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 13.02.2023 to 16.02.2023.

Further he has furnished CT- Scan Films marked as Ex.P.8 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.9.
SCCH-5 13.
Dr.Rajesh M.B., Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Meditech Speciality Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.13, disability assessment proforma marked as Ex.P.14, inpatient case sheet marked as Ex.P.15, MRI Film (4 in Nos.) marked as Ex.P.16, MRI CD marked as Ex.P.17 and previous X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.18.
Further he has assessed permanent physical disability for left lower limb is 34%.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has issued discharge summary and as per the report, petitioner is suffering from heart problem since 12 years, so that, he has undergone angiography.

Further deposed that, petitioner came to their hospital for left leg legamentear treatment and he has not sustained any fracture and such legamantear may take place even in SCCH-5 other that RTA cases.

He has also deposed that, he has not consulted Mathrushree Hospital Doctors prior to treatment or during the treatment and he has mentioned in his report as RTA on the basis of the information given by the petitioner.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 11% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 34% of lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 45 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.7, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the Anjan Murthy vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141019410/

Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1. Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.2,20,158/-.

In chief examination evidence deposed that, Rs.1,79,000/- has been spent for heart disease and for that amount, petitioner is not entitled and there is one day delay in filing of the complaint, that too,
petitioner is standing on national highway by holding cow, it is not permissible under law and prays to dismiss the petition.

Ofcourse in the cross-examination PW-2 who is Doctor, who given assessment of the disability to the petitioner has categorically admitted that, since 12 years petitioner is suffering from heart problem and he undergone for angiography and petitioner has came to his hospital for his left legamentear treatment and he has SCCH-5 also admitted that, he has not sustained any fractures and also admitted that, such legamentear may take place even in other RTA cases and he has not consulted the Mathrushree hospital Doctor prior to the treatment and he also admitted that, he has not suggested the petitioner for future treatment etc.,
20.

On perusal of Ex.P.12 discharge summary, in the said document PW-2 and other Doctors of Mathrushree Hospital categorically mentioned that, petitioner Anjana Murthy came to the said hospital for treatment of PCL injury and knee injury.

At the same time, in the said discharge summary dated 16.02.2023 it is mentioned that, 10 to 12 years ago angiogram is done to the Anjan Murthy, so the treatment taken to the heart disease is about 12 years ago and not in the 2023 nor in the accident year.

So the arguments addressed by the SCCH-5 respondent No.1 counsel with regard to treatment, noway supports his case, because on perusal of the evidence of PW-1 and 2 and arguments of the petitioner's counsel, I have no hesitation to believe that, petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.2,20,158/- for the treatment of the injuries caused out of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Ofcourse PW-2 has admitted certain fact as referred above, they have not sufficient to disbelieve the entire case of the petitioner, because the petitioner evidence is more probable than the Doctor evidence in the present type of the cases, because the petitioner is real sufferer out of the accident as well as injuries caused to him.
21.Per contra,except denial in the written statement, respondent No.1 has not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in SCCH-5 the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent No.1 has filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of him to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.120222223340040265 which is valid for the period from 25.11.2022 to 24.11.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 08.12.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of R2 shall go against R1, so that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the SCCH-5 rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

::ORDER

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,40,196/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Forty Thousand One Hundred Ninety Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
